research_question: In randomised trials of parenting or family interventions for children with conduct problems, does a personalised (tailored, adapted, or subgroup-matched) version of an intervention reduce child conduct problems at end of treatment, measured on the Eyberg Child Behavior Inventory (ECBI) Problem scale, compared with the standard non-personalised version of the same active intervention?
treatment_label: Personalised / tailored or subgroup-adapted parenting or family intervention
control_label: Standard non-personalised version of the same active parenting or family intervention
outcome_description: Child conduct problems at the first post-treatment assessment, measured with the Eyberg Child Behavior Inventory (ECBI) Problem scale (number of behaviours rated as a problem; range 0-36), mother's report preferred when multiple reporters are available. Extract post-treatment mean, SD and n per arm; convert SE or CI to SD where needed. Exclude the ECBI Intensity scale, follow-up assessments, other child behaviour scales and parent-level outcomes.
positive_direction: A positive effect means the personalised/tailored intervention produced fewer child conduct problems (lower ECBI Problem scale score) at end of treatment than the standard non-personalised version; i.e. a raw MD below zero on the ECBI Problem scale favours personalisation.
search_queries: tailored parenting program randomised trial Eyberg Child Behavior Inventory conduct problems
adapted versus standard parent training child disruptive behaviour randomized controlled comparison
personalised family intervention matched subgroup child conduct problems outcome trial
inclusion_criteria: Randomised trial (or randomised comparison) of a parenting or family intervention for children with conduct, disruptive, oppositional or externalising behaviour problems
Compares a personalised, tailored, adapted, enhanced-matching or subgroup-specific version of an intervention with a standard/generic version of a broadly comparable active intervention
Reports quantitative child behaviour outcome data at or after end of treatment, including an ECBI Problem scale score or data from which it can be derived
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic review, meta-analysis, editorial, commentary, opinion or purely theoretical/protocol paper)

No comparison between a treatment condition and a control/comparison condition (single-arm or pre-post only), or the comparator is a waitlist, no-treatment or treatment-as-usual rather than a non-personalised active intervention
No quantitative outcome data usable for an effect size (no means with SDs/SEs, t/F values, proportions or odds ratios)
Completely unrelated to parenting/family interventions for child conduct problems
moderators_to_extract: Type of personalisation (content tailoring, subgroup matching, dose/delivery adaptation, cultural adaptation)
Base intervention programme (e.g. PCIT, Incredible Years, Triple P, other)
Delivery format and setting (individual vs group; clinic, home, online)
Risk of bias / attrition rate and intention-to-treat vs completer analysis
effect_size_note: Pool raw mean differences in ECBI Problem scale points with a random-effects (DerSimonian-Laird or REML) model. Use only the first post-treatment assessment; do not pool follow-ups, ECBI Intensity scores, other behaviour scales or parent outcomes. Prefer mother-reported scores; convert reported SEs or 95% CIs to SDs (SD = SE x sqrt(n)) when SDs are not given. MD < 0 favours the personalised intervention, and effect signs are flipped so that a positive pooled value indicates benefit of personalisation.
